title: Site comparison preserves the support localization boundary
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $i:C\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:V=T\setminus C\hookrightarrow T$ be its open complement [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $F$ be an ordinary sheaf of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on the small etale site, viewed in degree zero in $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $F_p=\nu_T^*F$; identify $j^{-1}F_p$ with $\nu_V^*(j^{-1}F)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

Let $c_T^q$ and $c_V^q$ be the degree-$q$ global-section comparison maps induced by the derived adjunction unit [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology]. Let $c_C^q$ be the degree-$q$ map of the canonical support comparison $c^C_{T,F}$ of [lem-pur-support-site-comparison], with supported cohomology defined by the kernel-of-restriction right derived functor [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Let $\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q$ and $\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q$ be the connecting maps of the two support long exact sequences [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], using the same cochain/snake-boundary convention in the two topologies. Then the triples $(c_C^q,c_T^q,c_V^q)$ form a morphism between these long exact sequences. In particular, for every $q\geq0$,
$$
c_C^{q+1}\circ\partial_{\mathrm{et}}^q
=\partial_{\mathrm{pro}}^q\circ c_V^q:
H^q(V_{\mathrm{et}},j^{-1}F)\longrightarrow
H^{q+1}_C(T_{\mathrm{proet}},F_p).
$$
All squares, including the restriction and forgetting-supports squares, commute without an additional sign. These maps and squares are natural in $A_T$-linear morphisms of $F$; in particular all comparison maps and connecting maps are $A$-linear. No constructibility or freeness assumption is imposed on $F$.

source.place: Tag 09XP, label section-cohomology-support, displayed injective restriction sequence, distinguished triangle and its long exact sequence. Compatibility with the specified etale/pro-etale adjunction-unit comparison is an agent-formulated refinement of this construction; the tag alone does not assert this comparison.

proof.text: Use the fact that the open complement is a monomorphism in each site, and apply the generic site normalized support sequence to obtain δe and δp with both their normalization and their exactness on all bounded-below coefficients.

Apply the existing ordinary comparison-pullback open-unit theorem. Postcompose with the direct image of the canonical coefficient-isomorphism hom and cancel its inverse. This is the required SupportBoundaryOpenUnitNormalized equation.

For every degree-zero coefficient F apply the cochain realization lemma to the two normalized boundaries. Apply transported snake naturality to obtain the boundary square, and transported homology naturality to obtain the support-inclusion and restriction squares.

For each of the three comparison maps, its naturality square evaluated on a sheaf morphism in degree zero is exactly the final corresponding assertion. All maps already live in ModuleCat, hence are A-linear. The two constructed boundaries are themselves natural transformations.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09XP and homology.tex Tags 0117 and 08N7, realized by explicitly normalized cochain models and right-derived base-change naturality. The main proof uses independent injective representatives joined by a lifted chain map, rather than pushing a pro-etale representative forward or assuming comparison-unit invertibility.

The mathematics is correct. Step 1 pushes a pro-etale injective resolution forward with nu_*, which keeps it injective because nu^* is exact; this does not rely on inverse image preserving injectives. Step 2 holds because nu_* is evaluation at the same object, so the two complexes have identical sections and identical support kernels. Step 3 shows restriction to V is surjective for module injectives, via the free-presheaf monomorphism and Yoneda; this is elementary and correctly marked. Step 4: restriction preserves injectives because an open immersion is etale and weakly etale, and the torsion hypothesis holds because n*A=0 for n the characteristic of A. Step 5 identifies the three components with the unit-induced comparisons c_C, c_T and c_V. Step 6: boundary naturality is HomologySequence.delta_naturality, and there is no sign because both rows use the same snake on identical cochains. Edge cases C empty, C=T and F=0 all check out, and no SGA is cited. One C3/C4 fault, repaired: Step 2 took 'a represents the derived adjunction unit' from lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective.
